findings.reason: The protected source is already concise, conventional, and expert-interview quality. `frequencies`, `required`, `row`, and `value` state the fixed-domain counting invariant without indirection, and the threshold return avoids a redundant final scan. Set intersections or per-row sets would allocate more dynamic state without improving clarity or complexity, so no candidate materially improves the solution.

Strict increase prevents duplicate values within a row, so each increment means that one additional processed row contains the value. A count can first reach the required row total only while scanning the last row. At that moment the value belongs to every row; because the last row is traversed in increasing order, the first threshold-reaching value is the smallest common element. If no count reaches the threshold, returning `-1` is exact.

An independent set-intersection oracle and a separately implemented first-row membership control agreed with protected and immutable native sources on all 11 ordinary cases and all three benchmark tiers. Exhaustive enumeration covered 23,784 rectangular matrices with one through four rows, one through five columns, and every strictly increasing row drawn from values 1 through 5, with zero mismatches.

A further 10,000 deterministic schema-valid matrices generated with seed 1198 had zero disagreements. Coverage included 517 single-row, 528 single-column, 6,846 common-element, 3,154 no-common, 2,010 multiple-common, 1,575 minimum-value-common, 1,668 maximum-value-common, and 2,548 final-column-common inputs, plus explicit 500-row and 500-column matrices.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 1198, Python, and native entrypoint `Solution.smallestCommonElement`. Fresh authenticated evidence confirms the nonempty rectangular `m x n` matrix, strictly increasing rows, smallest value present in all rows, `-1` absence result, both dimension bounds through 500, value range through 10^4, two exact examples without explanations, and four hints.

The immutable native source remains bound to verified submission 2067921514 and is unchanged. Apart from the required class-method wrapper and type syntax, protected and native sources use the same 10001-slot table, row-count threshold, row-major traversal, increment, immediate threshold return, and absence fallback with identical algorithm and data flow.

Fresh evidence showed that the original 10/20/40 square tiers did not reject their intended explicit-membership control, which passed scaling at 0.76x. The repaired hidden tiers use two disjoint rows and scale column count 50, 200, and 500, remaining fully source-valid while separating the protected O(mn) scan from quadratic membership work. In three consecutive runs protected passed all 14 outputs and scaling at 0.97x to 1.01x; the correct control preserved every output but failed only scaling each time with excess growth +0.26 to +0.30.

The Approach matches the protected frequency table, strict-increase membership invariant, final-row threshold property, increasing-order early return, and `-1` fallback. Its O(mn) time follows from one visit per entry, and O(1) auxiliary space is correct because the 10001-slot value domain is fixed by the source constraints.

The modular Reference preserves exactly the two authenticated examples in source order with exact matrix and output literals, correctly records that neither has an explanation, and includes all five constraints and four independently worded hints. The former disjoint local example remains only as visible case coverage and is not presented as a source example.

A fresh authenticated Premium review found two unexplained examples, five constraints, four hints, and no image, table, diagram, note, or follow-up. `source_fidelity.json` binds every modular section to live description-content hash 80857f34c05f157e10894377cdfd052d2c7949d4d061557951f7e8434b532651 and validates without errors.

coverage: The first two visible samples are the two authenticated source examples in source order with exact matrices and outputs. Neither source example has an explanation, and the Reference does not invent one.

All 11 ordinary fixtures are visible samples or trials. Exact boundaries cover one and 500 rows, one and 500 columns, and values 1 and 10000. Material cases cover one or several common values, smallest selection, no intersection, one row, equal and unequal one-column rows, a late common value, and a value present in all but the final row.

The set-intersection oracle independently recomputed every expectation. Protected, native, and the explicit-membership control agreed on 23,784 exhaustive small matrices and 10,000 seeded legal matrices spanning absent, unique, multiple, minimum, maximum, and final-column common values.

The three hidden performance-only tiers use source-valid two-row matrices with ordered column-count sizes 50, 200, and 500, a 10x span. Protected passed scaling in three runs; the correct explicit-membership control retained all 14 answers but failed only the runtime verdict in every run.
